quiz.title: Unit 3 FRQ 2: Sinusoidal model from data (Topics 3.1 to 3.7)
quiz.headline: Build a sinusoidal model from monthly temperatures, use an average rate of change with units, solve the model, and reason about how the rate of change behaves.
quiz.promptTitle: Free response 2 · Sinusoidal model from data · graphing calculator
quiz.prompt: The average daily high temperature in a city, in degrees Fahrenheit (°F), is modeled by the sinusoidal function T, where m is the month number (m = 1 for January, m = 2 for February, and so on, with m = 13 for the following January). The table gives values of T(m) for selected months. The model reaches its maximum value at m = 7 and its minimum value at m = 1 and m = 13.
quiz.instructions: Part A style: a graphing calculator is required. Show the work that leads to each answer; answers without supporting work may not earn credit where work is requested. Angle measures are in radians. Avoid rounding intermediate values, and give decimal approximations accurate to three places after the decimal point unless the part says otherwise. Unless otherwise specified, the domain of a function f is the set of all real numbers x for which f(x) is a real number.
quiz.note: Original practice question written in the AP Precalculus free-response format (6 points, parts A to C). Scoring is self-assessed with the point-by-point rubric. It is not an official AP question or an official AP score.

scaffold.label: Show work
scaffold.text: Write the setup, such as the expression you evaluate or the equation you solve, before the answer.

scaffold.label: Use exact values
scaffold.text: Without a calculator, give exact values such as √3/2 or 7π/6, not decimals.

scaffold.label: Justify
scaffold.text: When a part says give a reason or explain, refer to the graph, the given values, or the context.

responseFields.label: Part A (i)
responseFields.prompt: A (i). T can be written in the form T(m) = a sin(b(m + c)) + d, where a > 0 and b > 0. Find the values of a, b, and d.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

review.label: Period, amplitude, and midline from data

responseFields.label: Part A (ii)
responseFields.prompt: A (ii). Find a value of c for the form in A (i). Show the work that leads to your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

review.label: Phase shift from a data point

responseFields.label: Part B (i)
responseFields.prompt: B (i). Use the model to find the average rate of change of T from m = 1 to m = 4. Express your answer as a decimal approximation and include units.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part B (ii)
responseFields.prompt: B (ii). Interpret the meaning of your answer to B (i) in the context of the problem.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (i)
responseFields.prompt: C (i). Use the model to find all values of m, for 1 ≤ m ≤ 12, for which T(m) = 72.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

responseFields.label: Part C (ii)
responseFields.prompt: C (ii). On the interval 4 < m < 7, is the rate of change of T increasing or decreasing? Give a reason for your answer.
responseFields.placeholder: Show the work that leads to your answer, then state the answer with any units or notation the part asks for.

rubric.label: A (i) a, b, and d
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for a = 20, b = π/6 (about 0.524), and d = 62. All three are needed.

rubric.label: A (ii) c
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for c = −4 (or any value −4 + 12k), with work such as (π/6)(7 + c) = π/2.

rubric.label: B (i) Average rate of change with units
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for (T(4) − T(1))/(4 − 1) = (62 − 42)/3 ≈ 6.667 degrees Fahrenheit per month.

rubric.label: B (ii) Interpretation
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: from m = 1 to m = 4, the average daily high temperature increases, on average, by about 6.667 °F per month. The interval and 'on average' are needed.

rubric.label: C (i) Solutions
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for m = 5 and m = 9. Both are needed.

rubric.label: C (ii) Rate of change with reason
rubric.guidance: Earn the point for: decreasing, because on 4 < m < 7 the graph of T is above its midline and concave down (T increases toward its maximum more and more slowly).

quiz.modelResponse:
A (i). Maximum 82 and minimum 42 give a = (82 − 42)/2 = 20 and d = (82 + 42)/2 = 62. Consecutive minimums at m = 1 and m = 13 give a period of 12, so b = 2π/12 = π/6.

A (ii). The sine function reaches its maximum when its input is π/2. The maximum is at m = 7, so (π/6)(7 + c) = π/2, 7 + c = 3, and c = −4. T(m) = 20 sin((π/6)(m − 4)) + 62.

B (i). T(1) = 20 sin(−π/2) + 62 = 42 and T(4) = 20 sin(0) + 62 = 62. The average rate of change is (62 − 42)/(4 − 1) = 20/3 ≈ 6.667 °F per month.

B (ii). From m = 1 to m = 4, the average daily high temperature increases, on average, by about 6.667 °F per month.

C (i). 20 sin((π/6)(m − 4)) + 62 = 72 gives sin((π/6)(m − 4)) = 1/2. For 1 ≤ m ≤ 12, (π/6)(m − 4) is between −π/2 and 4π/3, so (π/6)(m − 4) = π/6 or 5π/6, which gives m = 5 or m = 9. A graphing calculator confirms the intersections of y = T(m) and y = 72 at m = 5 and m = 9.

C (ii). The rate of change is decreasing. On 4 < m < 7, T rises from its midline value at m = 4 to its maximum at m = 7. The graph of a sinusoidal function is concave down above its midline, so T increases at a decreasing rate there.
quiz.alternateModel: A cosine form is also correct when the question allows it: T(m) = 20 cos((π/6)(m − 7)) + 62. In the sine form, c = 8 also works, since it differs from −4 by the period 12.
commonErrors: Taking the period as 6, the time from a minimum to the next maximum.
Using c = 4 or c = 7, which shifts the graph the wrong way or forgets that sine peaks at input π/2.
Giving an average rate of change without units or with the units reversed.
Giving only m = 5 for T(m) = 72 and missing the second solution.
